Check out the git tag OTP-29.1.3, and build a full OTP system including documentation. Apply one or more applications from this build as patches to your installation using the 'otp_patch_apply' tool. For information on install requirements, see descriptions for each application version below.
POTENTIAL INCOMPATIBILITIES
- An external DTD was automatically fetched by xmerl_scan which resulted in a scan of an untrusted DTD that may result in an out of memory crash.
  xmerl_xcan has now got a new option {fetch_external_DTD, Boolean} which default set to false to protect against this. This result in an incompatibility if one took advantage of that xmerl_scan auto fetched the external DTD.
  The secure way to use a DTD is to let fetch_external_DTD be false (default) and use doctype_DTD to provide the needed DTD in the call to xmerl_scan.

crypto-5.10.1
The crypto-5.10.1 application can be applied independently of other applications on a full OTP 29 installation.

Fixed Bugs and Malfunctions
- Fixed two bugs in the AES-GCM decryption fallback used when crypto is built against OpenSSL 1.0.1 through 1.0.1c: the ciphertext and AAD arguments were swapped, and an empty authentication tag was not rejected. AES-GCM decryption on these builds now behaves the same as on all other OpenSSL versions.
  Own Id: OTP-20381
  Related Id(s): PR-11927
- Added bounds checks to crypto:pbkdf2_hmac/5. The password, salt, iteration count and derived key length must now be at most INT_MAX, otherwise a badarg exception is raised.
  Own Id: OTP-20514
  Related Id(s): PR-11938
- When crypto was built against OpenSSL 3.x, crypto:generate_key(rsa, {ModulusSize, PublicExponent}) could generate a key with a different public exponent than requested on little-endian machines.
  Own Id: OTP-20515
  Related Id(s): PR-11939
- crypto:hash_final_xof/2 (SHAKE128/SHAKE256) now runs on a dirty CPU scheduler when the requested output is large. Before this fix, asking for a long XOF output could block a normal scheduler for a long time and hurt the responsiveness of other processes.
  Own Id: OTP-20551
  Related Id(s): PR-12200
> Full runtime dependencies of crypto-5.10.1
>
> erts-9.0, kernel-6.0, stdlib-3.9

erts-17.1.2
The erts-17.1.2 application can be applied independently of other applications on a full OTP 29 installation.

Fixed Bugs and Malfunctions
- Fix race between ets:delete/1 and exiting process auto unfixing the table. Could cause emulator crash.
  Own Id: OTP-20462
  Related Id(s): ERIERL-1338, PR-11908
- Fixed an issue where comparisons of maps were not deterministic between runtime instances; one node in a cluster could say A < B where another said A >= B.
  Own Id: OTP-20511
  Related Id(s): PR-11568
- A bug in the AArch64 (ARM64) JIT could crash the BEAM virtual machine when processing certain input. The flaw caused the runtime system to misuse a CPU register in some chained comparison operations, leading to a segmentation fault.
  One way this was triggered was by parsing XML containing an oversized numeric character reference (for example, &#576460752303423488;) with xmerl_sax_parser. Any application that passed attacker-controlled input through an affected code path could be vulnerable to a denial-of-service crash.
  Only AArch64 (ARM64) systems running the JIT were affected. The x86-64 JIT, interpreter (emu) builds, and 32-bit platforms were not affected.
  Own Id: OTP-20523
  Related Id(s): PR-11967, CVE-2026-115747
- A bug in x86 JIT that caused <<>> to be compared equal to some non-empty bitstrings has been fixed.
  Own Id: OTP-20525
  Related Id(s): PR-11954
- A bug that reduced garbage collection efficiency has been fixed.
  Own Id: OTP-20528
  Related Id(s): GH-11923, PR-11971
- Fixed binary_to_term to handle incorrectly encoded reference with Len=0. Could cause beam emulator crash instead of badarg exception.
  Own Id: OTP-20530
  Related Id(s): PR-12043, CVE-2026-116293
- Port commands with the nosuspend option could be executed by the port even though it had set itself in a busy state.
  Own Id: OTP-20534
  Related Id(s): GH-11941, PR-11942
- Fixed bug in term_to_binary(Term,[local]). Caused emulator crash if Term contained funs.
  Own Id: OTP-20545
  Related Id(s): PR-12148
- The ct_run command no longer crashes with a segmentation fault when -sname, -name, -browser or -ctname is given as the last argument without a value. It now prints an error message and exits with status 1.
  Own Id: OTP-20546
  Related Id(s): PR-12147
- Fixed binary_to_term for Erlang fun terms deliberately incorrectly encoded. Could cause the Erlang VM to abort due to stack exhaustion.
  Own Id: OTP-20555
  Related Id(s): PR-12182, CVE-2026-117642
- When erlang:open_port/2 with {spawn_executable, FileName} accepts the executable name and the args, arg0 and cd option values as binaries, the previous implementation did not check for embedded NUL bytes. Everything after NUL would be silently dropped. Now NUL bytes will be rejected with badarg.
  Own Id: OTP-20559
  Related Id(s): PR-12198
- Fixed binary_to_term of old FLOAT_EXT with an invalid string without zero termination. Avoid dangerous buffer overrun and instead fail safely with badarg.
  Own Id: OTP-20561
  Related Id(s): PR-12181, CVE-2026-120961
- On macOS, the runtime system could crash or hang when using a file operation on a file name starting with certain Unicode symbols.
  Own Id: OTP-20569
  Related Id(s): PR-12231, CVE-2026-125658

inets-9.8.2
The inets-9.8.2 application can be applied independently of other applications on a full OTP 29 installation.

Fixed Bugs and Malfunctions
- Fixed a vulnerability in the inets HTTP server (httpd) where a request header name could create a new atom in the atom table. Since atoms are never reclaimed, an unauthenticated client able to reach an Erlang Server Interface (ESI) URL prefix could grow the atom table with ordinary HTTP requests until the runtime system aborted when the atom limit was reached, taking down all applications on the node. Only servers with at least one erl_script_alias configured are affected. Servers without ESI, CGI scripts served by mod_cgi, and the httpc client are unaffected. When building the environment passed to an ESI callback, httpd now derives the {http_<header-name>, string()} keys from a fixed set of standard request header names instead of constructing an atom from the header name received. The documented mod_esi contract is unchanged for those headers. A header outside that set is now reported under http_other, which is already where a header whose name is not an existing atom has always been placed.
  Own Id: OTP-20458
  Related Id(s): GH-SA-7fjc-wcvc-vp96, PR-12262, CVE-2026-116382
